utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I briefly deal with two matters and I cut matters short. The first is that for P698 [sic] a new version was uploaded into e-court which would reflect the Chamber's decision concerning omission of an excerpt of that document. The new version was uploaded, as the Chamber understands, into e-court under 65 ter number 31640a. The Registry was already -- has already been instructed to make the necessary replacement and therefore will now do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then as far as P07072 is concerned the -- a new translation is there. I'll deal with that in more detail once we've heard the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just a small transcript correction, Mr. President. Line 15 indicates P698 and I believe the Court was referring to P6938.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I at least wanted to refer to. Good morning, Witness. Could I invite you to stand, Mr. Stanic. Mr. Stanic, before you give evidence I would invite you to make the solemn declaration that has been handed out to you already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Stanic. Mr. Stanic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Good morning, gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, would you please tell us slowly your exact name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Surname Stanic, name Milenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, did you at one point in time give a statement to the Defence team of Mr. Mladic [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I hear "Mr. Mladic" or did I hear "Mr. Karadzic"? Did you give a statement to the Karadzic Defence or to the Mladic Defence, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I gave a statement to the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court 65 ter 1D04317.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, you will see your statement on the screen before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the last page of it. In B/C/S could we see it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, on this page of your statement do you recognise the signature, is it yours?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The date which is handwritten on the left-hand side, is it the date that you wrote yourself in your own hand?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very briefly, Mr. Stanic, in the course of proofing before you appeared before the Court, did you share with me some details about your encounters with Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we call up in e-court 65 ter 1D04 -- 05326, 05326.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would only like to ask you, Mr. Stanic, this information that you shared with us concerning your encounters with Mr. Mladic and the details that you provided during the proofing with the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic and the answers you provided in the Karadzic case, today when you gave the solemn declaration in this courtroom would you provide the same answers to those same questions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have the disadvantage, of course, of not being present for all of the previous Defence examinations in which proofing notes were referred to or admitted, but I did not anticipate that there would be a 92 ter attempt for this. I have no particular objections with the Defence doing a measure of leading since they presented us with the proofing note, but unless this has been a practice in this case, I'm not sure either of the specific requirements of 92 ter have been fulfilled or that this is an approach the Court would favour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think usually -- I would say that proofing notes often where they were dealing with minor technical details, that they were not gone through, although sometimes the Defence also has chosen to go through them in all detail. I think it was yesterday that we heard that the end of a career of a witness was slightly changed by a couple of months. But here, as a matter of fact, Mr. Stojanovic, what we find here is encounters with Mr. Mladic which is perhaps at the core of this case which were announced in the 65 ter summary where I think not a word was found in the statement that was tendered under Rule 92 ter. Therefore, it's certainly a bit uncommon what you're doing at this moment, certainly not in line with what is usually done. The Chamber has not had the advantage, Mr. Tieger, to even read the proofing note, at least I've not seen it. It may be that it was sent. Was it sent, Mr. Stojanovic, to Chambers staff? It may well be. I may have --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe we did provide to you and the Prosecution this material, and I was prepared to talk to Mr. Tieger and go through the answers Mr. Stanic gave me during proofing. And I would not like to depart from the procedure and the material we have obtained during proofing, that was the understanding we had with Mr. Tieger. This was only a way to make it happen faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may have missed it, Mr. Stojanovic. Could you tell us when it was sent to the Chambers staff, this proofing note and as I now understand the revised Defence exhibit list for the witness. Could you give us any details?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this was sent yesterday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday morning. Let's have a look, 28th --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, while we were in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we'll verify that whether it was done or not, at least I now have it in a printed version before me. Perhaps you touch upon -- it's the core of the case, it's encounters with Mr. Mladic, that you deal with every paragraph very briefly, not necessarily to read it all. The first one is that the witness in his ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber considers the statement to be a new statement, as a matter of fact, it touches upon matters which do not appear in the original statement. Therefore, we'll see how you work with it. You have tendered in your 92 ter motion the original statement given to the Karadzic statement. We'll decide on that and we'll see how you proceed with the remainder. We know by now that the witness has -- during proofing has apparently given a new statement. We leave it in your hands how to proceed, but we'll first focus on what was tendered -- what was submitted in your 28th of October --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stanic, my last question before we started to deal with this formal problem: Would you today, after giving the oath in this courtroom, provide the same answers to the same questions that had been put to you by the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic and would these answers be to the best of your knowledge, truthful, and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, those answers were truthful and my answers would not be any different.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the statement of Witness Milenko Stanic which is 65 ter 1D04317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection against admission of that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that statement would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D04317 receives number D884, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. D884 is admitted into evidence. Witness, may I take it that you made a mistake when you said that that statement was taken one year ago because on the basis of the date we find in it, it is two years ago that it was taken? February 2013.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's when I was here at the Tribunal and some time before we did the proofing. I was here around 15 February 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I have one question. Something appears which is quite extraordinary in this statement which is now admitted and I'm seeking your explanation for it. Between paragraph 42 and 43 it reads: "Information elicited on the 16th of February, 2013, translation provided by Karadzic Defence." That appears just in the midst of this document and I wonder what it is that paragraph 43 would be different from the first 42 paragraphs? Could you explain to us what triggered this to be part of this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, according to the information I got from the witness, before talking to Mr. Karadzic during proofing before he appeared in the courtroom that day, 16 February 2013, the witness added this information which is contained in paragraph 43 and the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic added it subsequently to the statement that was admitted into evidence in that case. And it concerns a person called Ferid Hodzic, TO commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if that's the case, when was the original statement taken if this is just paragraph 43 being proofing? When was the witness interviewed? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I was told, it was the day before in a room in the Detention Unit and that interview was continued on the 16th of February and it was put in writing and made a part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that the most part of your statement was taken one day and then the other day, the day on which you signed, that a paragraph was added?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, the proofing took a long time. I provided most of the facts in 2012, towards the end of 2012. Of course I talked to the Defence team in the field and read back the statement. And when I came to testify here I reviewed it again, and the Chamber in Karadzic accepted the statement without any problem and there were no objections either by the Prosecution or the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember who took the statement -- I mean, when you were interviewed already in 2012, was that by Mr. Karadzic or was that by his team or members of his team? Do you have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Members of his team on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And were you then interviewed by Mr. Karadzic himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, during proofing I met with Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was the day before you gave testimony; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In writing. I can't say exactly. It's possible. It was either the day before or the day after, but it was within one day of testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Stojanovic, does this then mean that paragraph 43 has not been translated by CLSS?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, from what I know about the way the Defence team of Karadzic works, they immediately write down things in English and that is how they provided the statement in English directly to the Chamber in Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the way they work, but what is the answer to my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, the CLSS did not translate their statements. They translated their own statements and submitted them as such to the Trial Chamber. But of course, take this with a grain of salt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What then is the significance of making this remark: "Translation provided by Karadzic Defence," if it is no departure from normal practice?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't know how to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. These, however, are matters which if you tender a statement you should be aware of. If it catches our eyes within a second, then it surprises that you have not given it more thought. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like to tender also the two accompanying documents, 1D03128 and document 1D04318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections? These were originally the associated exhibits to the initial statement. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3128 receives number D885 and document 1D4318 receives number D886, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D885 and D886 are admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Stanic, today when you have given the solemn declaration here in the courtroom, do you stand by the remarks that you made during our proofing regarding the encounters and contacts you had with General Mladic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, they have not been tendered as an exhibit. They are not before Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, I believe they were. They have a number, 65 ter 1D05326, proofing note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They have not been admitted into evidence yet. Until they are admitted into evidence you cannot talk about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Let me then tender 1D05326 to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we say it's a new statement. Please introduce the information in that statement viva voce so that all doubts as to what it is about -- because we received it now but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour, that's how I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I will ask you this: During war-time events did you have any meetings with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, a number of meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you able to tell me, if you remember, in 1995 where these meetings took place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: There were several of them, and I can confirm that I participated in two meetings about which General Mladic made some entries in his war diaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us what was the topic of those meetings, the talks and discussions in which Mr. Mladic participated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry to interrupt the examination, but I thought it was best to head off some confusion before it became embedded in the record and had to be disentangled with further questions. Based on the proofing note, I understand the two meetings the witness is about to talk about to have taken place in 1992 not 1995. So I don't know whether or not that was simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, from what I read until now it says that he had a greater number of meetings starting from mid-1992. If the two specific meetings in the second paragraph, Mr. Stojanovic, if they took place in 1995, then, first of all, the proofing note doesn't say that at all. So would you then first, instead of introducing in your question the year 1995, first establish when it was that the various meetings referred to in the first and the second paragraph of the proofing note took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I got 1991 in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I want to ask you this: The two meetings that you are discussing, when did they take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where were they held?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The first one in Vlasenica, at the Municipal Assembly seat in Vlasenica. The second one was held at the Municipal Assembly seat in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, again, it is a new statement so when I refer to it, I did so because it was given to us and it was entirely unclear about the year. The appropriate way of introducing this kind of evidence if, for example, you want to elicit the evidence as we find it in the second paragraph of this document, which is not yet in evidence, is: Have you met General Mladic at various occasions? And then you can, for example, mention a year. And then you elicit the evidence viva voce even if you have in the back of your mind what you know and what is before us, that is, the proofing note. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you now is this: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what the topic was of the first meeting in 1992 in the Municipal Assembly building in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The entire leadership attended the meeting, the leadership of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, and there were a number of members of the Main Staff. We informed the members of the Main Staff about the ongoing security and political situation in the municipality. While preparing for the meeting, our Secretariat for National Defence prepared a report about the degree of mobilisation and we informed the members of the Main Staff about that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what General Mladic said in his address on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: General Mladic asked us for a greater degree of engagement in the process of mobilisation, for greater support in the supply of the army units, and he pointed to some impermissible acts that he said he would deal with and try to root out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber when the second meeting was held, the one in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: After the meeting in Vlasenica, I think that this is around the time of late June 1992 or possibly early July 1992 - I'm not sure if I will get the date absolutely correct - and it was in the municipal building in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what did General Mladic talk about at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by military commanders and the entire political leadership of the municipalities belonging to the Zvornik region. General -- the General particularly talked about a decisive battle against paramilitary formations that were particularly active in the Zvornik area during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally I would like you to tell the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second. Did he talk about paramilitaries in Zvornik -- Serbian paramilitaries or Muslim paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he spoke about Serbian paramilitary formations in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to end with this question, Mr. Stanic: The other meetings where you had the opportunity to meet General Mladic, what was his position and what did he most frequently talk about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I never noticed or observed General Mladic issuing any kind of instructions to expel Muslims after military attacks nor any type of commission of war crimes. He often spoke about our internal problems during these meetings in the Serbian republic, and in particular he criticised the problems and the functioning of the Ministry of the Interior. He often criticised certain deputies as well who often criticised the army without any valid arguments for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stanic for these responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask a question. In what capacity did you attend the meetings in Vlasenica and in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica and also for a brief period as the president of the Autonomous Region of Birac which included a number of municipalities in the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And thank you to the witness, Your Honours. I have no further questions for the witness so, by your leave, I would like to read the summary of the statement of Witness Milenko Stanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and whatever you wanted to have additionally admitted is now elicited viva voce so we can put aside at this moment the proofing note. Please read the summary, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Milenko Stanic was elected to the post of president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica after the first multi-party elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina and he remained at that post with some status changes until 1993, when he was appointed to the post of minister of trade and tourism in the government of the RS. When he was performing the duties of president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, according to the agreement on the division of power with the SDA, Izet Redzic, a member of the SDA, was elected as president of the Executive Board of the municipality of Vlasenica. From the beginning right after it was formed, the authorities did not function properly and there were frequent differences about the question of implementing the referendum on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina about the position towards the JNA and mobilisation, about personnel issues, and the documentation of the Secretariat for National Defence. Aware that the Muslims were moving towards independence and secession from Yugoslavia, the Serbs approached the formalizing of the idea about the Serbs remaining in the SFRY and the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Vlasenica. The agreement between the Serb and the Muslim people was verified and signed at the Assembly session on the 13th of April, 1992, at which time it was also adopted. However, in the implementation of the decision, the leadership of the SDA backed out of the agreement so that only the part of the decision relating to the forming of the municipality of Milici was actually carried out. At the same time, with these political attempts to settle the crisis in a peaceful way, the population was leaving the municipality of Vlasenica en masse, first of all, Serbs and then followed by the Muslim population in the direction of Tuzla. Together with Redzic, he personally went to Tuzla and called on the Muslims to return to Vlasenica and to continue their life together. On the 21st of April, 1992, the TO was mobilised with the task of securing buildings of key significance and to prevent looting of property. This task was carried out without any fighting and without any casualties. In his statement he talks about the reasons for the forming of the Crisis Staff in Vlasenica, the problems in its functioning, and the later forming of the War Commission, and tasks relating to organising the accommodation and transport of the civilian population, i.e., those who were leaving and those who were arriving at Vlasenica, about the purpose of the Susica facility, and about his knowledge relating to events in the villages of Zaklopaca, Drum, Pijuci, Dzambici, and Bare. Your Honours, this is a brief summary of the witness's statement. We have no further questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. I am just -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, Susica is dealt with where exactly in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, Your Honours. Paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check again. Yes, that is about buildings and houses and not about -- I now understand that you say the explanation of - and let me read it - the Susica facility, you are purely talking about houses and people staying there for a while. Nothing about -- it's not referring to any detention facility or something of the -- like that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours, as it states in paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's -- well, summary is not evidence so we don't have to further be concerned about that. Then, Witness, having now gone through your examination-in-chief, you'll now be cross-examined, you'll be cross-examined by Mr. Tieger. You find Mr. Tieger to your right. In a minute he'll be standing. Mr. Tieger is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I commence the cross-examination, I would simply note, as I indicated to Mr. Lukic before the beginning of the court session, that Mr. Stanic did receive a 90(E) advisement in the Karadzic case. Mr. Lukic indicated -- don't want to speak for him, but that he broached the subject generally with the witness as I think he routinely does, and the witness indicated he didn't need such a warning. But given the fact that it was given in the Karadzic case, I just wanted to bring it to the attention of the Court and leave it in the Court's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The practice is in this Chamber that -- especially if these are Defence witnesses, that, first of all, the Defence thinks about it and discusses it. If, Mr. Tieger, you at any point in time feel that a 90(E) warning would be appropriate -- and of course I don't know what kinds of questions you are going to put to the witness and not knowing what material you would have which would make you believe that 90(E) warning would be there. But if you find there is a point where it might be wise to do so, then the Chamber will do so at your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. As a general matter I think the nature of the cross-examination implicates issues that would give rise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- to such an advisement in the similar manner as the examination in Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you therefore say is: In view of the questions I'm going to put to the witness and in line of what my material tells me, it would be wise already to do that right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, rather than waiting for the specific questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll do that right away. Witness, I'll read to you Rule 90(E) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. It says: "A witness," that's you in this case, "may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question, but testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." So if you think your answers would be of an incriminating nature for yourself, you may ask not to answer that question. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, we have about ten minutes until the break, so we will be covering a few questions. So you know the timetable, we'll be adjourning for 20 minutes after that. You mention at paragraph 5 of your statement that you were chosen as president of the Assembly, which I understand to be the highest position in the municipality, and that Mr. Redzic was selected as the chairman of the Executive Board. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say what the highest-ranking position is. It was a system of local authority, pre-war system, where the Executive Board had broader competencies than the president of the Assembly. The president of the Assembly was not a mayor with the mayor's competences. He was a deputy, first among deputies, and he presided over the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. The Executive Board then was - as the designation indicates - an executive body and was the municipal equivalent of what the government was at the republic level; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No. The Executive Board was the local government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think there was just a translation misunderstanding. That's what I was trying to indicate. Now, in paragraph 13 of your statement you refer to the adoption of a decision and the joining by the Vlasenica municipality of the Birac Autonomous District in December of 1991. Now, that body that is referred to here as the Autonomous District was not an ethnically neutral or general multi-cultural regional body, but it was one of the regional bodies known as Serbian Autonomous Districts or Regions; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: That body was called the autonomous area or region of Birac. At the Assembly session, the deputies asked that it be -- or a number of the deputies ask that it be named the Serbian autonomous region; however, at the request of deputies from other parties, the reformist party and the SDP, explained that the area with such a name should be left open for the Muslims -- deputies of Muslim ethnicity to also join the body who were in favour of the preservation of the federal state. It's true that the body functioned for a very brief period of time and it comprised only deputies of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I understand that it was -- it's your testimony that the designation of the body in the vote that was taken in Vlasenica was altered to make it more palatable to Serbian opposition members, but the reality is that this body was known to others including the Bosnian Serb Assembly as the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who imagined what, but I could just go by the facts. In Vlasenica, we as members of the Serbian Democratic Party did not have the necessary majority to reach such a decision. We needed the support of four deputies who were members of the former communists, this is the SDP party, and from Markovic's reformists, meaning the reformist party. And it was their explicit request, in order for them to support such a decision, was to call it the Autonomous District and not the Serbian Autonomous District. And I've already told you what their explanation was. I think that that was a good proposal; however, the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina was not like that and that was evident from the referendums, that the line was complete and that all Muslims mostly were in favour of leaving the federal state and that all the Serbs were in favour of the preservation of the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One document before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn to 65 ter 02334.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I asked you about the position of and the understanding of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. This is an excerpt from the 2nd Session of that body on the 21st of November, 1991 - at page 32 in English and page 33 in Serbian - and reflects the Assembly's decision on the verification of the declared Serbian autonomous provinces in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the Serbian autonomous regions in Krajina, in Herzegovina, and in Romanija-Birac encompassing municipalities such as Han Pijesak, Pale, Sokolac, Vlasenica, and Sekovici. So this is a reflection, Mr. Stanic, of the understanding by, among others, the Bosnian Serb Assembly that these bodies were Serbian autonomous regions or districts; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Evidently this is that type of decision. In the -- on the ground, however, there were different situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Well, when we return we'll look at some documents reflecting the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, the previous question where I think you were asked about how the Assembly looked at it, not the local Assembly. And then you said: I don't know how they looked at it. That's not entirely consistent with the answer you're giving us now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I think I understood the timing correctly and we would be breaking now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Stanic. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could tender 65 ter 02334 before we move forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a very long document, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand -- in conformity with the Court's practice, Mr. President, which I understand was to either tender this excerpt separately or we can hold it in abeyance until we identify the full collection of excerpts from this Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit that I do not remember at this moment whether we had reserved a number for the 2nd Session. If not, then I leave it to you. You know better how you're going to use this same document in future, we do not know. So if you think there will be considerable follow-up, then I think it would be good that we tender it but that later you'll make the excerpts of all the portions in it you dealt with, and otherwise to tender it separately as an excerpt now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I would -- maybe I can answer that at the break. I just want to check with a couple of people to see if they have in mind some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait until after the break. We'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you said you would inform us after the break about the use of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I would -- for now I would ask to have it, 65 ter 02334a, include - and I mentioned this to Mr. Lukic at the break - pages 1 through 4 and 32 through 34 of the English and the same in the Serbian. I don't believe there's any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they have been uploaded as such? Not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we reserve a number awaiting the upload of what you just told us would be uploaded. Madam Registrar, the number reserved would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number reserved for document 65 ter 2334a will be P7077, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, the SAOs, the Serbian Autonomous Districts or regions, were established commencing in September 1991 pursuant to guidance and direction from the SDS republic level; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I do not remember having any guidance or direction of that kind, but following the situation as it was unfolding in Bosnia-Herzegovina and noting the obvious fact that people were trying to overturn the federal state that we shared, I believed, together with other politicians in Vlasenica during the ongoing negotiations about demarcation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that it was necessary to take a position on the issue and to enter the negotiations as a municipality where the majority of deputies to the Assembly would be in favour of remaining within the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 65 ter 31906, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can the witness please answer the question that was put to him. Were they established commencing September 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say the date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when each region was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the witness gave a long answer not focusing on what you asked him as a matter of fact -- well, the first line was, but apart from that. I do not know whether we want to and whether you want to listen to many explanations which are not directly related to the question. And I would not be surprised if you say: You have answered the question. Witness, could you please try to focus your answer on the question because the last question was about whether you acted upon guidance and you said you don't remember any guidance of such kind. That's an answer to the question. And then what else was on your mind and where you thought it would be wise to take a position or not was not asked and perhaps Mr. Tieger is interested in it, perhaps he's not at all. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And thank you for that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The document in front of you, Mr. Stanic, as you can see, is first a cover page sent by Rajko Dukic, the president of the Executive Board of the SDS of Bosnia and Herzegovina, referring to the decision on the appointment of the regionalisation staff and a request for realisation of all activities relating to regionalisation through that staff sent to all the municipal boards and city boards of the SDS on September 13th, 1991. If we turn the page, please, we can see what Mr. Dukic is referring to and that is the decision on the appointment of the regionalisation staff pursuant to the decisions and conclusions made at the counselling of municipal, regional, and republican organs of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina held on 7 September 1991. And the decision continues: "The Staff for monitoring the implementation of the decision on the proclamation of autonomous regions ..." is noted and specified below. That is a reflection, Mr. Stanic, is it not, of the republic-level direction to the municipalities to take affirmative steps regarding regionalisation and in particular the proclamation of the Serbian Autonomous Districts or Regions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just asked it, Mr. Stanic. This is a decision, isn't it, by the republic level sent to the municipal bodies to implement the conclusions and decisions at the counselling held on 7 September and in particular the proclamation of SAOs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I can say I've never seen these decisions. As far as I can see, they were sent out by the Serbian Democratic Party. Whether this decision reached the Municipal Board of the SDS I don't know because I was not the president of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you're suggesting to this Court that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the witness tells us that he never received guidance, he doesn't know anything about it. We have documentary evidence and if the witness doesn't know anything, then perhaps we should -- of course you can put a little bit to the witness and then to see whether he may have forgotten about some matters, but let's not spend too much time on --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Happy to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with a witness who apparently does not know about these things which are documented at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Happy to tender and move forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will first read the number and then I will hear you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31906 receives number P7078, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 26, line 21 of the provisional record, the Prosecutor says it's a decision to appoint SAO, the Serb Autonomous District. I should like to hear where we can see that in the document the Prosecutor is showing, that it's about a Serb SAO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If the language of the document is inconsistent with the phrasing of the question, I yield to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is Autonomous District. I think it is -- but doesn't change your --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. The point of the question was much broader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's hereby then corrected. I think the -- let me just see. Yes, I think from the answer of the witness, yes, it -- from the answer of the witness it seems that he has not been confused by any inaccurate quoting of the document which, indeed, talks about autonomous regions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me deal directly with the question His Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think now we have ruled on the objection so now it's time to decide on admission. Admitted into evidence. And of course I'm talking about P7078. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And let me deal briefly with a question His Honour Judge Moloto asked you, and that was whether or not Serbian Autonomous Districts began to be proclaimed in September, that is, shortly after the 7 September meeting that we just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that connection, if I could turn to 65 ter 16200.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is an article from "Javnost" of 21 September 1991. If you look at the upper right-hand corner of the page in Serbian we can see an article on life as Serbian Autonomous District and the article begins: "Two Serbian" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you read that, could you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of the 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The article commences: "Two Serbian autonomous districts and one autonomous region were declared this week: Old Herzegovina, Romanija, and Bosanska Krajina ..." And then the article goes on to discuss the -- some aspects of the underlying reasons given by the author. This is a reflection, Mr. Stanic, isn't it, of the reality that in the relatively immediate aftermath of the 7 September meeting, Serbian Autonomous Districts or Autonomous Regions began to be declared, consistent with the direction that was provided in the previous exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I've already answered once. I don't see why I should answer your questions ten times. Your questions are the same. I said it could have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in September or maybe after September. But I can say that in December --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, if there's any objection to the question, it comes from either the Defence or from the Bench, not from you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger, and you may --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 16200, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 16200 receives number P7079, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, whatever designation you put on it for whatever reason, whether to induce opposition deputies to join the vote, the reality is that the purpose of these bodies, these regional bodies, and the purpose of the regional body for Birac was to advance the interests of the Serbian people; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The Serb positions were made clear in the referendum, and if you look at it in that context, they gave 100 per cent support to staying in the shared state. And if we look at it that way, then your remark is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at it a bit broader than a very narrow, limited reference to the referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So perhaps we could turn to 65 ter 16184a.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Stanic, reflects minutes of a -- of the -- of THE meeting of the Assembly of Autonomous District Birac held on February 5th, 1992, in Milici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It says "autonomous region." On top of the English page: "Minutes of meeting. "Second session of the Assembly of Autonomous Region of 'Birac' ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not the President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour, I'm sorry. I was focused on the document and misspoke. My apologies. Thank you for that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I want to track through some of the comments made at that meeting. First of all, in point 1 of the meeting we see that: "Milenko Stanic, chairman of the Executive Council of the Autonomous Region of Birac" - and we need to move it so you can see, Mr. Stanic, to page 2 of the Serbian - "explained the Executive Council Operating Programme ..." and opened debate on the programme. Now, as we continue through we see Mr. -- during the course of the discussion about the programme, we can see where the focus of that discussion goes. So Mr. Jovicic states - if we scroll down on the English, please - that existing means of -- excuse me, that "the economy of the region should be linked with the economy of neighbouring regions of Romanija and Semberija and with the economy of Serbia ..." Mr. Dukic states --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we also perhaps read, then, the line that follows which may be relevant: "The available media should be used only if they satisfy the needs of Serb people." Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I did want to bring that portion to the witness's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dukic states that there should be information on the current political situation in the republic, in particular regarding the referendum that the Serbs should abstain from. He goes on to say that: "The Serb people should establish their own rule in the region and even further." Mr. Tesic states a little further below that: "This should be just the beginning, a starting point for further work on the programme to make it better meet the interests of the Serbs," et cetera. We see Mr. Savkic below talking about the relationship between the proposed economy and the economy of Serbia. These references, among others, Mr. Stanic, reflect the fact that this body was focused on fulfilling the interests of the Serbian people. That was the purpose and effort of this body; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Those were the discussions among the Assemblymen, and as you can see, they're mostly about economic topics, because the Assemblymen were all Serbs and it's logical that they were concerned with Serb interests.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Tieger, could we just turn over the page of the English one to see the conclusions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 16184a receives number P7080, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, we mentioned Mr. Dukic earlier in connection with the distribution of the 7 September -- or of the decision arising from the 7 September meeting. Mr. Dukic, as noted in that document, was the president of the Executive Committee or the Executive Board of the republic-level SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a while he was the president of the Executive Board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And he was also the co-ordinator for SAO Romanija-Birac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that connection perhaps we could look at two documents quickly. The first is 65 ter 07908. These are the minutes of the 8th Session of the Executive Committee of the SDS of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on 6 September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 6 February --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: February 1992. And if we turn to the third page in English, item 4, I believe that's also the third page in Serbian but let's check.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We see that there is a recommendation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's not the correct page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Item 4. There. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We see a discussion about the impact of the formation of the Assembly of the Serbian people and the ministerial council rendering the need for or eliminating the need for the existence of a regionalisation staff. And in line with that, the recommendation by the Executive Committee to charge people with responsibility for the accomplishment of regionalisation on the ground. And making the recommendation that the following individuals be charged with such responsibility in various regions, including Mr. Dukic in Birac and Semberija. And perhaps it's easier if I -- I turn you to another document reflecting the culmination of that recommendation - that's 65 ter 12934 - which reflects a document of 24 February 1992 by the SDS Executive Committee and specifically a decision that Mr. Dukic be appointed as the designated member co-ordinator for the SAO of Semberija and Birac. So those two documents, Mr. Stanic, reflect what you indicated previously, that Mr. Dukic was the co-ordinator for the Birac body?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was the co-ordinator but in my statement I did talk about my relationship with Mr. Lukic [as interpreted], our relations were not that good, and at that time -- or actually, before the beginning of the civil war I didn't have any particular communication with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you talking about Mr. Lukic or about Mr. Dukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajko Dukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber unanimously could not imagine that you would have a bad relationship with Mr. Lukic, so therefore all three of us immediately intervened. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 7908 receives number P7081 and document 12934 receives number P7082, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7081 and P7082 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, this Trial Chamber has received evidence that on February 14th, 1992, at a large plenary, Radovan Karadzic activated the second level of Variant A and B, that is, the instructions of 19 December 1991, that's P3774. Now, what the evidence in P3774, a recording of that plenary meeting, indicates is that Mr. Karadzic explained at page 5 of that document in English and page 4 in the Serbian that now more important than meetings and proclamations is to "gain the real situation, the factual situation on the ground." He explained that Serbs have the "right" to "introduce the stage number 2 and functioning of your areas and relying on your own forces to absolutely defend yourselves from the independent Bosnia and Herzegovina." That's at page 7 of the English, page 5 of the Serbian. And said further: "Please, that" -- this is at page 24 of the English and page 18 of the Serbian. "Please, that is why we called you today, to intensify, to introduce the second level, and to intensify the functioning of the government at any cost and on every single millimetre of our territory." Now, I'm going to ask you if you recall being present at that meeting, Mr. Stanic, and I ask that in particular because Mr. Dukic opens the meeting by noting, and this is at page 1: "Apart from the members of the Main Board and the Executive Board, we invited to this meeting the presidents of SDS Municipal Boards, presidents and members of regional boards, presidents of Assemblies, Executive Committees of municipalities, where we have them and our officials in government where we have them and our officials in government and party organs, as I can see the majority came, maybe even all of you, and I thank you." So do you recall being present at this meeting along with all of these other officials of the party?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I cannot be definitely sure whether I attended that meeting or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I assume, however, that whether you were physically present or not, that someone - perhaps even Mr. Dukic - conveyed to you exactly or in general terms what had happened at this important plenary session?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It's possible that somebody from the party went to the meeting. Dukic did not convey to me any instructions because, as I said, we didn't have much communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's try it in more general terms. Whether it was Mr. Dukic or another member of the party, either from Vlasenica or from the regional body of Birac, you were made aware, were you not, of the intensification of activities related to gaining the real situation, that is, the factual situation, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We had more contacts at the regional level, and certain information and procedures I got from the colleagues from the local Assemblies that were functioning at that regional level.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And although your statement at paragraph 42 might be read as suggesting that you are entirely unfamiliar with the content of Variant A and B, as you indicated in your Karadzic testimony - and if you wish, I can direct your attention to the specific portion - you had heard of the document or at least partially aware of its contents and heard people discuss it at a minimum.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: As I said, I received a part of the information from representatives of the local Assemblies that probably operated pursuant to such instructions. I personally don't recall the document or its exact provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, four days after Mr. Karadzic called for "intensifying the functioning of the government at any cost and on every single millimetre of our territory," the - and that's at page 24 of the English of P3774 and 18 of the Serbian - four days after that the 1st Session of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO was held to advance the take-over of power in the area of the Birac SAO; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I cannot state the exact date. As for the Executive Council, two sessions were held and two Assembly sessions of the autonomous region and that's where the whole process ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 1 -- sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dukic, Witness, you were not asked how many times they met. You were asked whether the Executive Council decided -- was held to advance the take-over of power. Do you remember that that happened in one of those few moments where they met?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At those two meetings we talked about the issues of the regions that should become part of the autonomous region and that we would nominate in future negotiations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- about the peaceful solution of the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina, those that wanted to remain in Republika Srpska. So I cannot really answer such a specifically put question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you can give the details of what was discussed. If you say: I don't remember when their advancing the take-over of power was discussed, then tell us that you don't remember and we'll move on. Apparently you have some recollection on subjects that were discussed, but this one, if you don't remember, please tell us. You don't remember? Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, if we could call up 65 ter 16187.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This document is the minutes of the 1st Session of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO held on 18 February 1992 in the premises of the Municipal Assembly beginning at 1000 hours. And we see there, Mr. Stanic, that you as president of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO chaired the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we turn to the conclusion at page 3 of the English, and if you turn the page in Serbian as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: "Conclusion. "In order to take over power in the area of the Birac SAO as efficiently as possible ..." And then it goes on to identify some issues in relation to that objective. So this is a reflection, Mr. Stanic, of what I had asked you earlier, that is, that four days after Mr. Karadzic gave the instruction to "intensify the functioning of the government on every single millimetre of our territory," the Birac SAO Executive Council met to implement precisely that objective, that is, the taking over of power in the area of Birac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We already were in power. Why would we want to take over power? I had the Assembly majority in Vlasenica. We had our own chief of the public security station and our own commander deputy. What is being discussed here is the issue that I mentioned and that is the central topic of all of our discussions, both at the Assembly and in the Executive Board, was how to remain, how to join that part of Bosnia and Herzegovina that would recognise federal laws and remain in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. We had a commission that would be working on these questions because we were concerned that if there were no activities we would be pulled into a centralised Bosnia and Herzegovina, but the one that none of the Serbs wanted to accept and support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before we deal with that I have one question. This was the first meeting of the Executive Board. You signed the minutes. Could we go to the last page, page 3 in e-court. Did you adopt those minutes? I see there's no signature but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The minutes are not signed because there were errors by the person who drafted the minutes, because it was SAO and it was actually the autonomous region as reflected in the decisions of the Assembly. So the person taking the minutes made these errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have corrected minutes been drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that should have been so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether it should have been but whether it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question is not what you think but whether you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What if I don't know now? What answer can I give?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, then you tell us that you don't know. It's a simple as --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. I'm not 100 per cent sure. But I think I drew the minute-taker's attention to that error and asked that it be corrected, but I don't know whether I signed that -- those minutes or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which suggests that there would be another version of the minutes of this meeting. If that could be found or is it -- if it's anywhere in the collections held by either Defence or Prosecution, the Chamber would like to know whether they were ever changed. Because the minutes were, what we saw a minute ago, adopted in the 2nd Session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We will certainly do a double-check, Mr. President, but I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Witness, you earlier told us you had no idea what people would imagine. Now, if the minute-taker again and again and again in this document talks about a Serbian autonomous region, then -- and if you explained to us that you have drawn his attention to that mistake, then the answer that you could have no idea of how the autonomous regions were perceived, isn't it true that on the basis of this, what you call a mistake, let's just leave it to that, and having seen all the other documents about Serb autonomous regions, that you indeed you could imagine how the autonomous regions were perceived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me to evaluate what people were thinking and I cannot do that. Probably your remarks are correct, but I cannot figure out or say what people were thinking. So in that sense perhaps my answer or my opinion would not be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, sometimes people express how they perceive something, and if that frequently happens, you may gain an impression of how other people perceive things. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both yes and no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain the no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way people think is different. In their thinking, people are sometimes guided by their interests or wishes, and reality, however, is very often different. I know that it was the wish of the Serbs to have their own territorial unit in Bosnia and Herzegovina that would remain as part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and probably the majority thought along those lines. Bosniaks or Muslims were thinking of their own state that they would control by a majority. And so that was their way of thinking. So from that aspect, everybody would be looking at these documents in their own way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what I'm asking you, as a matter of fact, is that everyone expresses as his perception or his opinion that A would be better than B, then you can gain an impression of how people perceive A compared to B. Just to give an example, if all the Serbs say: We would rather stay in a federal Yugoslavia, I agree with you, and that's the no, that they may think otherwise, they may all want to separate from the federal Yugoslavia. But that's apparently not how you understood it. What I'm saying to you more or less is: That where you earlier said that you could not imagine how people perceive something, that in everyday life we orient ourselves on how people express that they perceive matters or what opinion they have, and that in that respect I'm asking you whether having seen all of this, whether indeed you had no idea about how the autonomous regions were perceived as put to you by Mr. Tieger, that is, that they were mainly for the Serb interest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the Assembly comprised all Serbs and that it was logical for them to represent Serb interests, but I do leave room for deputy Muslims who would possibly opt to support such a concept and that the Assembly membership would be filled by them. You also saw the deputies' discussion during the Assembly, all Serb ones. So there isn't too much discussion at that session about Serb interests, but in questions of life are interested, issues pertaining to enterprises and work. It was logical that we were thinking about connections with Serbia because we were turned towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm an economist and I'm not a philosopher so I cannot respond to questions about who thought what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That question was not asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put another question to you, Mr. Stanic. Mr. Stanic, you said corrections had to be made to these minutes with respect to the term of "Serbian autonomous region." Were other corrections made as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say right now. I cannot answer with a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger put to you one sentence under the heading "conclusion," and I read it to you again: "In order to take over power in the area of the Birac SAO as efficiently as possible ..." Was that sentence corrected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm wondering why you as the chair of this meeting and the person who is supposed to sign minutes, reading this sentence answered to Mr. Tieger: "We already were in power. Why would we want to take over power?" I really don't understand. Why does such a sentence appear in these minutes you were the chair of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that sentence is taken out of context of the conclusions that go along with that sentence. I mean, minute-takers were often less educated, while the minutes from the Assembly sessions of the SAO were made by a person with a law degree. Here we're talking about a typist who finished secondary school, three years of secondary school. So it's very likely for such mistakes to be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is your explanation. I heard that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you tendered that document, Mr. Tieger? We have not assigned a number to it yet or have we? No. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 16187 receives number P7083, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think we have time to follow-up on the question His Honour Judge Fluegge asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He directed your attention to the rhetorical question you asked in response to my question and your comment was: "Why would we want to take over power?" And then you went on to mention that the central topic was how to join the part of Bosnia and Herzegovina that would recognise federal laws and remain in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Mr. Stanic, the fact was that you as president of the SAO Birac government or AO Birac government, however you want to put it, were determined to ensure that under no circumstances would the laws of an independent -- sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina affect any Serbian household; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that commitment of ours was not in dispute. We had the support of the people for this position via the referendum and so that was our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is misquoted. It says an independent sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina. The date of the minutes is the 12th of February, 1992, but the document of the Prosecution has a different date as to the proclamation of an independent state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe the question was the witness's determination to prevent an independent -- the laws of an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina from affecting Serb households whenever that transpired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore -- but could you say where exactly then Mr. Tieger misquoted the document, what word he used which is not consistent with what is in the document, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Tieger on page 45, line 14, 15, and 16, and 17, spoke about an independent sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina in the context of the conclusions from the meeting of the 18th of February, 1992. Bosnia and Herzegovina became independent after this date according to documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Haven't you listened to the response by Mr. Tieger? Mr. Tieger asked what -- whether there was a determination to ensure that never such a thing would happen, which doesn't require that there is already an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is aiming at it never happening that in an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, so therefore the objection is denied. And I would advise you to carefully listen to the response to -- of Mr. Tieger before you -- and to my comment on that before you raise the matter again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break perhaps but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're near to a time for a break if this would be a suitable moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was going to show a document that's directly related to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that and take the break after.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This will be very quick, Mr. Stanic, before the break. It's an article entitled: "Overnight to Serbia," from an issue of Politika on 5 March 1992, dateline Zvornik Vlasenica 4 March --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which part of the B/C/S version, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's top right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'm just going to refer to one portion of the document where you're quoted, Mr. Stanic, and I think that's the second paragraph to the end where you say: "We shall under no circumstances let any" -- he referred to Bosnia and Herzegovina's independence, that is, the possibility of the event of a declaration of its independence and state that: "... we shall, under no circumstances, let any of its laws, regulations, or similar, enter a Serbian household, said Milenko Stanic, Prime Minister of the SAO Birac." So just to confirm, Mr. Stanic, that's a reflection of what you said before about your determination to prevent the possibility of the laws of a sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina from entering a Serbian household?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: This Bosnia and Herzegovina that was being created --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- by Alija Izetbegovic you see here --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, excuse me, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, first could you please answer the question, whether this reflects what you said. You were not asked yet to explain what you said, but first whether it reflects what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a lot of free interpretation by the journalist here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this reflect what you said? And if not, would you then tell us, not to explain what you meant, but tell us what you then said if this is not what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the laws of this independent and sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina that was being created by the Party of Democratic Action, SDA, headed by Alija Izetbegovic, could not operate on the territories inhabited by the Serbian people. And there are some more mistakes here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The government, the Executive Council, the SAO, the autonomous region was being created, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
