utterances.text: Can you explain why in this article again you are referred to be Prime Minister of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Birac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can I put it? I introduced myself by my proper title, president of the Executive Council of the Autonomous Region or the Autonomous District. I don't know how the journalist perceived it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, but I just -- if I may, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, the explanation is pretty clear, isn't it? As you explained before, the Executive Council at the municipal level, and also at the regional level, is the equivalent of the government and so -- and at the government level in the republic, the president of the government is called the prime minister. And so that's why this designation appears here; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's an executive body. It's an executive council and in journalist practice they often call it the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31916 receives number P7084, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is leaving the courtroom, I would just mention that the excerpts from 65 ter 02334 have been uploaded and provisionally assigned P7077.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was done already -- oh, yes, we reserved that number for it. Yes. Admitted into evidence, P7077. We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I take it you've come to deal with the matter which was still on the agenda. Now in order not to make you a hostage in this courtroom, I give you an opportunity to address the matter immediately so that you are free if you wish to leave again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As I understand it, we are here in relation to the document D758 and that one is the -- it was a handwritten statement of an individual that also -- the original also contained a typewritten telex of the same statement that had some changes in the date, some typographical errors in the date, and the name of the individual in question was incorrectly stated in the English translation. We have received from CLSS a new translation. It has been uploaded into e-court, but I see that it still has the same wrong name for the individual, the first name, as -- it's missing one letter. And as to the dates, the date discrepancy is in the two original documents, one handwritten and one typewritten, such that the CLSS would not be able to change that date. So we're left with two originals that have a discrepancy in the date, one says 1953, one says 1956. I don't know what Your Honours want to do with that. We could perhaps keep it -- split it into two documents maybe and then have a translation made of the second document or I don't know how to address that where we have two B/C/S originals from the original source that have differing dates for what purports to be the same source document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I could imagine that the parties agree that if there are two original documents about an event that certainly there must have been an event, and therefore that both versions -- where it may be very difficult at this moment to decide on which is the most accurate one, that we admit both into evidence and that the parties can argue whatever they want on the basis of the two versions and make us believe which version is better than the other one and why. If that would be a solution, Mr. Tieger -- because let's not forget there are two documents in existence, and to that extent, of course, you can have in evidence two documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I wasn't privy to earlier discussions, but it sounds like a very Solomon-like resolution -- sort of actually the opposite of a Solomon-like resolution but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ivetic, where you said there was still something with the name, is that -- is there a translation error in it or is it -- or transcription error or is that also one of the divergent elements of these two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, both the handwritten and the typewritten original have the gentleman's first name as S-e-n-a-i-d and the English translation has S-e-n-a-d. So it's either a typographical error or a mistake as to the name. I did not want to have us change the official translation but we could also do that just to address that one clear discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would -- if it's just one letter in a name, then perhaps we could live with that, all parties are -- unless it would be a matter which would create a lot of dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't see it creating dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Especially now that we've done it on the record it hopefully will be clear in everyone's minds what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we can do two things. If we make -- if we separate them, then of course already in terms of numbers one would easily lose sight of the other one. So another possibility is to have them all, both with the wrong translations in evidence under one number, and that we then -- the description would then be: "Two handwritten and typewritten original versions of," and then what it is. And that we have two B/C/S pages and two -- one B/C/S version with English translation, the other B/C/S version with English translation, have everything all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honours, we still do not have an official CLSS translation of the handwritten. I have not yet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- got word back on that, so we can't yet make it formal. But if we do it that way, I will make sure that both get into e-court and both get linked to the appropriate original so we can tell the translations apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I want to assist as much as possible while Mr. Ivetic is in the courtroom. So let me say that insofar as the resolution of these translation issues is concerned, that makes perfect sense to me. I apologise for not being more conversant with this particular issue and if the -- if the underlying issue was related to -- in any way to anything more than the translations, that is, if there was a some sort of provenance issue or authenticity issue or anything else, then I'm not in a position to speak on that. But as I say, in terms of the solutions the Court has devised on the spot for these translation -- not translation but these smallish discrepancies we've been talking about for a document that is otherwise coming in, then I'm in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thought that was the only issues that we had with the document when we MFI'd it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's from November so my memory's a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do the following: The translations will be verified. Both originals will be part of the exhibit with verified translations for each version we'll finally then admit into evidence, unless any of the parties will come up with any other disputed matter in relation to those documents. If we proceed like that and if you would let us know when everything would be uploaded, then we could proceed like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question here. Is it the position that in fact the typewritten document was typewritten by the same author of the handwritten one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours. I think as I recall from the witness who was on the stand, he wasn't sure if that was done by the same individual or if someone else in the police where the statement was taken had prepared the typewritten version after receiving the handwritten version. I believe that's my recollection of the testimony of the witness as to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's my recollection that the witness testified that he thought that a colleague would have done it. That is my recollection, but again I'm not giving a guarantee for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But logic and this explanation seem to suggest that, in fact, the handwritten one would be the original and the other one is a transcription. Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but of course in terms -- when I say "original," I mean original language from the original source. They both came to us as originals in the B/C/S language together, and then of course the CLSS does a translation. And I think they only did a translation of the typewritten one, assuming that the documents are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- identical, which we now find they may not be which is why we need to seek the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do understand that. The point I'm making is the author would probably have written in his hand or her hand and somebody who speaks the same language would have typed exactly what was typed there and probably made a mistake in typing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the handwritten one seems to me on logic to be the original and the one that should be relied on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But as far as I understand, we have not explored this issue from that point of view yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we only noticed that there was a translation issue and there were two originals. And whether now the transcribing person intentionally changed it or whether -- what the purpose or the thoughts behind it are or whether it's just a mistake has not been explored. And I think it's in that area where I suggested that if any party would like to argue anything on such matters that we would hear from them, but that is not a reason as such not to admit both, both documents originating from a source. I do not even know whether the typewritten version was the first one and then copied in handwriting. That's still -- theoretically still a possibility as well. We have not explored that. Once it's in evidence, the parties may argue whatever they want about the probative value of each of the versions and what it exactly would prove.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to confirm, Mr. President, I appreciate the conditional nature of the Court's discussion about this so far, I have now confirmed that the original objection to the admission of this document did not revolve around the issues we've just discussed, that is, the -- but instead, on the issue of whether a sufficient foundation was laid and the information about the document, the more conventional types of objections that have been made to documents of this nature. That can be found at transcript 28028 through 29. And so we're -- well, you've resolved part of the potential -- the major part of the issue still remains as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- raised by the Prosecution at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now after this discussion, Mr. Ivetic continues to take care that translations are there, proper translation, everything is uploaded. And then you will consider, Mr. Tieger, whether the objections still stand; and if they do, we will decide on those as part of our decision on admission apart from the other technical aspects. I leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, may I then be excused from the courtroom to attend to other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the whole purpose, Mr. Ivetic, to not to wait for any later moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Stanic. We needed a bit of time for administrative matters so you had to wait a little bit longer. Mr. Tieger will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, just to bring you back to where we were, we had been discussing before the adjournment the issues surrounding the conclusion about taking power and the determination that the laws of a sovereign and independent Bosnia would not enter Serbian households. By the end of May 1992, the government of the SAO Birac had passed a decision on -- or at least had resolved the issue of the determination of the borders of the region and had passed a decision on the "safe moving out of the Muslims." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We discussed that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that connection if we could call up P3737.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a "Javnost" article dated 6 June 1992 about reporting on decisions of 30 May 1992, indicating in part: "The Government of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Birac determined the borders of this region on 30 May ..." And goes on to note it sent an invitation to the representatives of neighbouring municipalities. And it further notes: "At the same time, a decision was passed on the 'safe moving out of Muslims from that area' ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads "moving," not "moving out," but -- at least that's what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, correct, "safe moving of Muslims from that area ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that was the -- so this reflects the decision that you confirmed a moment ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: All the municipalities in the region had a problem because there were many implications from the populace to move out and to go to other areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. You start explaining what you consider relevant to explain, whereas Mr. Tieger puts a question to you and we would first like to hear an answer to that question. And if any further explanation is required, the parties will ask for it or the Bench. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. So the -- just if you -- I'll give you a chance to explain if that's necessary, but I would appreciate, as the Court indicated, an answer to my question and that is: This article reflects the decision that you confirmed a moment ago when I asked you about that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: This is a journalistic story.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I asked you about whether or not by the end of May the Government of SAO Birac had determined the borders of the region and passed a decision on the safe moving out of the Muslims, and you confirmed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Or you confirmed that you discussed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's be clear on that, although then -- already then you didn't ask -- answer the question. Did you only discuss it or was any decision taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no decision. We discussed both that and the other issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, you say looking at this article which states clearly that a determination was made and a decision was passed, you state: "This is a journalistic story." Now, when asked about this article in the Karadzic case you stated something of a similar nature, saying you didn't know what "Javnost" was and what this was about; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we did not talk about that in the Karadzic case. A different attorney was on the side of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, was it discussed in the Karadzic case, irrespective of who asked you the questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, your comment was wrong. The question was: "Now, when asked about this article in the Karadzic case ..." That was the question. It didn't refer to who asked you that question. Mr. Tieger. And then Mr. Tieger summarised what you said, that you came up with similar comments like that you didn't know what "Javnost" was and what this was all about. Is that what you said at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question. You're asking me to say yes or no to a question that can't be answered with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31909.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's your testimony in the Karadzic case, Mr. Stanic, and I want to turn your attention to what you said at page 43, transcript page in Karadzic 34024. "Q. This is a 'Javnost' article of the 6th of June, 1992. So when they make reference to the decision made by the government of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Birac, that didn't -- you're saying that this newspaper must be wrong as well? "A. I am seeing this document for the first time. I would need to review it in detail. 'Javnost,' I don't know whose magazine that is and what is the source of information like this --" So that was your testimony about -- in connection with this article when first asked in the Karadzic case, Mr. Stanic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, I want to take a look at this mysterious "Javnost" that you purport not to know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, can we turn to 65 ter 14321.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document dated 13 September 1990 which shows us the origin of "Javnost" under the heading: "Decision to launch the Javnost ... newspaper ..." and it goes on to describe its -- the objectives for "Javnost" as providing information, among other things, about the SDS as a political factor. So this document confirms, does it not, Mr. Stanic, that the -- that "Javnost" was launched by, established by, the SDS, this is signed by Dr. Karadzic, for the purpose of expounding the views, among other things -- for the purpose of expounding, among other things, the views of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I never said I didn't know what "Javnost" was. I said I was seeing this newspaper story for the first time. That's the mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you said more. Could it be read to the witness, Mr. Tieger, could you -- I don't have it on my screen any further at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is what you said to the Trial Chamber in the Karadzic case: "'Javnost,' I don't know whose magazine that is ..."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I think I didn't say that. Maybe if the question was put to me, maybe it didn't specify that it was published in the "Javnost." I know what "Javnost" is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Witness, are you telling us that what is recorded is not accurate? Then we'll check it on the basis of the audio because as it was read out to you, you clearly referred yourself to "Javnost" as it was recorded. And then you said: "I don't know whose magazine that is ..." So you yourself used the name and you yourself are recorded as having said: "I don't know whose magazine that is," whereas today you tell us that you know what "Javnost" is and whose magazine that is. If you say: That's not what I said at the time, we'll verify it because such a clear contradiction should be verified before we draw any conclusions. If you say you didn't say it, then we'll verify it. Please tell us whether we have to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw this text for the first time, the one that was published. I don't recall any questions regarding "Javnost". If it was put to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, a minute ago you said you didn't say this. You also said that you do not whether "Javnost" was part of the question. "Maybe if the question was put to me, maybe it didn't specify that it was published in the 'Javnost.'" As we read it to you, it's not only that the question was about "Javnost" but even you yourself referred to "Javnost" as the magazine you didn't know what it was. If you say that's what -- I accept that that's what I said, then we take that. If you say: No, that's not what I said, then we'll verify on the basis of audio. Do we have to verify it, yes or no? That's my question. Do you still deny that you said that at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need to look at the transcript of that trial in detail in order to make sure. So my answer is: I knew what "Javnost" was but I saw the text for the first time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's all clearly recorded there. It's just the two lines, you don't have to read the whole of the transcript, it's just verification of those two lines. Do we need to verify it on the basis of the audio? And if you say -- if you don't give an answer to that question, as you didn't do two or three times, then we'll have it verified anyhow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I gave the answer. I know what "Javnost" is but I don't know the text. It was the first time that I saw it. That was my answer. If it was different in the previous session, then I would need to know the context in order to know why I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why you said that, that means that you admit that you said it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not accepting it. I'm just saying that the question was perhaps unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be verified on the basis of the audio. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. Stanic, the context is that you were asked about an article in "Javnost," which we see in P7077 is referred to as the Official Gazette of the Serbian people, which states that the government of SAO Birac made a decision on the safe moving of the Muslims. And you responded by saying: "I would need -- I'm seeing this document for the first time, I would need to review it in detail. 'Javnost,' I don't know whose magazine that is." That's the context. And now the Court is asking you whether you admit that you said that or we need to go back to the tape and have it verified?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: There were about ten "Javnost" publications. Perhaps I was not told that it was "Javnost" that was published in Pale and that's why I said I don't know the context in which the question is put, but now I gave the answer to your question. I know what "Javnost" is but I did not see that text.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, we've heard enough about what you said about this matter and the Chamber considers it best to have it verified on the basis of the audio. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and the government of the SAO Birac determine the borders of the region, or do you dispute that too?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We proposed the towns and citizens that would become part of the area and we proposed that to the Government of Republika Srpska. We proposed that as the basis for future negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you didn't simply discuss it. You determined what you considered they should be and then you raised it at the republic level; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We couldn't determine that because we were not authorised to do that. We just reviewed it on the basis of the deputies comprising the Assembly and their proposals as to which regions could become part of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's cut matters short again. Earlier you said: We didn't decide, we discussed it. Now I do understand that you discussed it and that resulted in proposals that were made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I failed to tender 65 ter 14321.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14321 receives number P7085, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm going to turn your attention to one of the meetings you talked about when asked questions in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's at P353, page 248 of the English and 246 of the B/C/S. That's the meeting in Zvornik -- and when I referred to 246 of the Serbian, that's in the transcribed version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We see at that meeting, Mr. Stanic, that you began, once you had the floor, by saying: "We have defined the western borders in the area of the Birac region" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that reflect the discussion and determination that was reflected in the article regarding May 30th or had further steps been taken toward the definition of the boundaries of the area of the Birac region between May 30th and this meeting on June 30th?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We proposed the boundaries. "Defined" seems to indicate more it was a decision. We could not suggest or propose a decision, it was not in our remit, but we could suggest the municipalities, the areas that could become part of Republika Srpska. The general wrote here, "definisali," "defined," I don't think that I used that term, but I used the term "predlozili smo," "we suggested."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. That's one part of what was discussed in the Javnost article. Let me turn to the other part and that is the decision on the safe moving of the Muslims which you say was not a decision but merely a discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that respect I'd like to call P190 -- yes, P190, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is an order from Commander Andric of the Birac Brigade dated 31 May 1992. "Pursuant to the decision of the 'Birac' Serb Autonomous Region government which regulates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of the 'Birac' SAR ..." Just like the Javnost article, Mr. Stanic, this is a reflection of the fact that the Birac government, Serbian Autonomous Region government, issued a decision on the moving or moving out of the Muslim population from its territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I state that it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So both the Official Gazette of the Serbian people Javnost and Commander Andric, the very day after the decision, referred to a decision which according to you had never happened; is that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the final item on the order in P190 states that: "The Prime Minister of the 'Birac' SAR is to establish contact urgently regarding negotiations on the exchange of prisoners." Now, as we've established before, the reference to prime minister of Birac SAR is a reference to you, Mr. Stanic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It is nowhere recorded that a soldier can order the president of the Assembly what to do. What he wrote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, whether it could be written, whether there was any authority to do that, that was not the question. The question was whether you agree that the reference to the prime minister of the Birac SAR would be a reference to you. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the signatory meant, I don't know. It's possible that he meant me, but he could not have issued these orders to me on any basis whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, again you think it necessary to add what you find important, whereas the question simply was whether he referred to you. You've answered that question that he possibly has done so. Next question, please, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What this indicates is that you were either to receive a copy of this so that Andric's concern that you undertake action regarding exchange of prisoners can be communicated or that he had already communicated with you about it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I saw this document when I came here to testify in the Radovan Karadzic case for the first time. It was not addressed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please answer the question again, otherwise we'll have to do without your testimony. If you don't answer the questions, then we'll just look at the documents and have to do, unfortunately, without your testimony on the matters you were asked about. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, Mr. Stanic, that nobody, either Major Andric personally or an emissary conveying this concern, communicated to you the concerns about the perceived need for exchanges of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Your question was: Did you receive this document? And I said no. And I'm also saying that nobody conveyed to me, including Mr. Andric, that a document like this exists. I saw it for the first time when I came here to testify in the Karadzic case. I don't know. Perhaps there were problems in the interpretation, but I cannot answer differently to the questions that are being put to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, who was the prime minister of Birac SAR on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the president of the Executive Board. I already stated that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot confirm that now. I said that they had two Executive Board meetings and two Assembly sessions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about sessions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and I think that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about sessions. I want to know if you have been the prime minister or the president on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about those meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you about -- stop --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- because after that -- after those meetings there were no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please, I'm not asking about any meeting. Have you been the president on the 31st of May, 1992, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure that the autonomous region was working at that time. I think that it had stopped working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was your position on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was very difficult to elicit this answer from you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger, but I would have one very simple question. Carefully listen to the question and answer it directly. Did anyone discuss with you or were you in any way involved in negotiations on the exchange of prisoners briefly after the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the municipality of Vlasenica we had formed a commission which contacted the Muslim side, but at the regional level there were no such negotiations and there was no commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask about a level, I didn't ask whether a committee on the other side was established. So I do understand that implicitly you're saying that you were involved at the municipal level in negotiations or at least communications about the exchange of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not personally. Not as a municipal official or a regional official, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not officially, unofficially what did you do, you personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you were not officially involved. Then I'd like to know how you were then involved if not officially. What then exactly was your involvement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't participate in it. I didn't take part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you do? If you say: I didn't do anything in this respect, then it would have been easier that your previous answer would have been: I was not involved, I never discussed it with anyone. Did you personally do anything in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With this, no, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Tieger, let me just clarify a little point here. Judge Fluegge asked you a question: What was your position on the 31st of May, 1992? You then said that you were president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica. I ask you a question. On that same day, 31st of May, were you also not the president of the Birac SAO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date when the -- that Assembly stopped functioning is not specifically known. At that time there were no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Executive Board or Assembly meetings being held at that time. We had stopped working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I don't understand your answer because you say the date when that Assembly stopped functioning is not specifically known. Now, you -- in the same breath you say that the Executive Board or Assembly meetings were being held at that time. You had stopped working. You can't say you didn't know, you don't know the date, and then say on that date you were not working. Those are two inconsistent questions -- answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Executive Council did not work because the organs did not convene. After this second session of the Assembly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to make sure that we are clear, can you just answer my question directly, yes or no. On the 31st of May, 1992, were you not the president of the Birac SAO? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those organs after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again I'm going to stop you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the second session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. I'm insisting on whether -- just say yes or no. Were you on the 31st of May, 1992, the president of the Birac SAO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not divested of that function ever because the organs never convened. The organs died off, they ceased to exist. For as long as they functioned, I had that post --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I stop you -- no, no, no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the last session was held and after that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Look, I stop you, I stop you. The record will show that you don't want to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, in late May and June 1992, you knew very well that the number of Muslims who were being detained and imprisoned was mounting and becoming a problem, as reflected by the concern we see from Andric in his order.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: We had the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For example, in the other one of the meetings with General Mladic that you referred to in your testimony earlier this morning in direct examination, that is, the June 25th meeting, you told Mladic that: "Over 800 prisoners, 200 of whom are women and children who were brought last night, pose a problem."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: In preparation for the meeting with the Main Staff, I received information from the president of the Executive Board that last night a few buses had arrived with prisoners who were placed at the secondary school. I informed the General about this. I did not know the exact number, but at the meeting one of those people who were present mentioned these numbers in the secondary school or the total number. We did not have the precise information. I don't think that anyone at that meeting knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, by that time the Susica camp had already been established; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: As I said, that was a reception centre. In the beginning it was a reception centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is the camp that Major Andric orders be set up in Vlasenica in item 1 of his order of May 31st?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Evidently that was not specified. At the time the army -- well, perhaps that was -- actually, it wasn't because General Andric belonged to units of the Yugoslav People's Army, which later transformed. And some of those members remained in the region and he probably meant the buildings that were owned by the Territorial Defence, or rather, the army and those were the ones in Susica. The secondary school centre was our problem where also that night a certain number of prisoners were brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So these prisoners were brought to the school rather than Susica because Susica was already full itself?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I don't know that that was so. I just received information just before the meeting that there was a substantial number of prisoners in the secondary school centre. I think the director of the secondary school centre asked the president of the Executive Board to submit information about that so that he could prepare the secondary school to begin work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And whatever you call Susica, reception centre or camp as Andric did, you knew by June 25th that there were hundreds and hundreds of Muslims detained in Susica or present in Susica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I didn't know the numbers, but I did know that there was a reception centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the reason there were hundreds of people in Susica and hundreds of people taken to the school in Vlasenica is because of Andric's orders to move women and children out of Muslim villages and take the men to collection centres; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I don't know that that was the only reason. I think that this order of Andric's referred more to the problem of prisoners from the area of the Kalesija municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you say you don't know whether that's the only reason. It was one of the reasons, I understand from that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was told we break at 1.20. I guess we're there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we're there. Could the witness -- we'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the Chamber, I have a small request, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Depends on what it is. If it's appropriate, please put the question to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It concerns our work and the adjournment. I've been here since Saturday. I've come to testify and I'm prepared to work for the next three days uninterruptedly but on Monday I have obligations and commitments at work that I cannot postpone. So I would appreciate it if we could continue working until we finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- we'll consider whether that's possible. You certainly would have assisted us by directly answering the questions because it took quite a lot of time to take you back to what was really asked. But we'll consider it. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, in this context could you give us an indication as to where we stand in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I certainly -- I'll finish -- I believe I'll finish today, although, as the Court has noted, my projections have been skewed by the nature of -- well, the indirect responses. But I'm still trying and I had anticipated being able to finish well in advance of the end of the session. That's not quite as certain, but I'll do my best to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you give us an indication, as matters stand now, how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it would take more than two to three minutes, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we try to conclude the evidence of this witness today so that we can meet his wishes to return. We'll take a break and make it a bit shorter now, take a break of 17 minutes. We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we've considered your request. Everyone will do their utmost best to conclude your testimony today. You certainly could help by just directly answering the questions and only answering the questions. And if we fail to do that, we'll continue not until Monday. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I had asked you about the mounting problem of hundreds and hundreds of Muslims detained and whether or not the Andric orders were responsible for that. In that connection let me show you two of those orders. The first is 65 ter 31907. This is an order dated the 26th of May, 1992, which directs, among other things: "Move women and children out of the Muslim villages to Kalesija and Gracanica, whereas the men are to be taken away to collection centres." And then if we could look quickly at P466, an order two days later, another order from Major Andric, this one the 28th of May. In item 6 we see the provision: "The moving out of the Muslim population must be organised and co-ordinated with the municipalities through which the moving is carried out. Only women and children can move out, while men fit for military service are to be placed in camps for exchange." These two orders, Mr. Stanic, produced the ever-increasing problem with the number of Muslim prisoners, some of whom were brought to Susica, some of whom, as you earlier noted, were initially at least brought to the school; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 31907.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31907 receives number P7086, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, we discussed the decision of the Birac SAR government regulating the moving out of the Muslim population, reflected in the 31 May Andric order [Realtime transcript read in error "article"] and the 6 June Javnost article. The moving out of the Muslims was, indeed, precisely what was envisioned by republic-level and Birac-level officials in order to define the borders of the Serbian state; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at what the president of the SDS Executive Board and the co-ordinator for the Birac region said in late July 1992 at the 17th Assembly Session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's P4581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, when you referred to the text signed by -- on the 31st of May by Andric, that was an order, isn't it? It is not an article as recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I certainly intended to say "order." Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said "order."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's turn first to pages 71 through 72 in the English, and 73 through 74 in the B/C/S. So we turn to 71 first in English and in B/C/S 73. Better -- okay. If we turn back one page in the Serbian, please. In the Serbian, not the English. So in the Serbian we see the beginning of Mr. Dukic's speech. Thank you. Now we see the beginning in English. Now if we turn to the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The speech starts at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. There we see Mr. Dukic talking about borders and he says: "We say that borders are drawn in the field. The people draw the borders, you must admit the state of facts ..." And he continues, and that's in the middle of the page in English you can see: "So the option is to take at least as much as belongs to us and I will tell you that we have not even come close to that ..." And if we can continue on to the next page in English and in Serbian, please. And perhaps one more page in the Serbian. Mr. Dukic had earlier asked: "So I'm asking you, gentlemen, why we expelled all Muslim judges from Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Zvornik," and he concludes with his description saying: "If we move further there is Birac which is 100 to" -- he had been talking about Bijeljina at one point. "If we move further there is Birac which is 100 to 108 kilometres away and has 120.000 Muslims - that is how many there were, but I hope that has at least been halved - and 90.000 Serbs." That's a reflection of the understanding as expressed by the president of the SDS Executive Board and the co-ordinator of the Birac region that drawing the borders means the reduction of the Muslims within the areas defined as Serbian; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I cannot comment on what Rajko Dukic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He was a leading republic-level official. He was the co-ordinator of the Birac region who was at meetings with you. He's telling the Assembly, the Bosnian Serb Assembly what the objective is and what he hopes will be accomplished, that corresponds with what we see accomplished in the orders that we looked at a few moments ago. That's a reflection of the common understanding regarding the need for moving out of the Muslims from the areas that were to be Serbian. Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Muslims left Vlasenica under different circumstances, different from what you're trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, you've already acknowledged that the Andric orders, at least in part, were responsible for the mounting number of Muslims who were detained in Susica and, as you're well aware, later moved either to Batkovic or exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as we see now from Dukic, that's the implementation of a particular desire and objective, to reduce the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It's possible, but I can't comment on his contribution to this debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, in paragraph 40 you state, that is, paragraph 40 of your statement, you state that: "We were not even able to ask the opinion of the leadership in Sarajevo and later in Pale on any problems because the telephone lines were mostly down and travelling on the roads was not safe." And then you further state that you "often went to other municipalities and consulted them in order to establish how they resolved certain problems." Now, first let me briefly address your representations with respect to communications. The fact is, Mr. Stanic, that communications were considerably better than you suggest here, that you received information from Pale and you in Vlasenica got information back to Pale during the period April, May, and June?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Many people lost their lives on those roads. As to your assessment, our communications may have been better compared to some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look very quickly - and I say "quickly" in a continuing effort to conclude today if we can - at some of those communications and I want to show you first a series of three documents relating to the appointment of Mr. Djokanovic, the war commissioner who's mentioned in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the first one would be 65 ter 16217. This is a document dated the 10th of June, 1992, it's Djokanovic's appointment by Dr. Karadzic as commissioner. And it refers also to the decision on the establishment of war commissions of 10 June of the same date. The next document I want to show you is P3737 -- sorry, 3735. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 16th of June, six days later, and reflects the appointment of the War Commission in Vlasenica municipality by Dr. Djokanovic and you pursuant to the decision of the Bosnian Serb Presidency six days earlier. So on 10 June, Dr. Karadzic makes a decision. On 16 June, you and Djokanovic appoint the War Commission; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to P3046.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document the very next day, that is June 17th, in which Dr. Karadzic confirms the appointments of the members of the War Commission named in the 16 June document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the chronology is: On the 10th of June, Pale issues a decision, that is, Dr. Karadzic. On the 16th of June, Vlasenica issues a decision, that's you and Mr. Djokanovic. And on the 17th of June, Pale, that is, Dr. Karadzic, confirms the decision. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And let me tender 65 ter 16217 in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 16217 receives number P7087, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One more short series that are this time two documents reflecting communications between Pale and Vlasenica. If I could first have P3982.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 29th of April, 1992, emanating from the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac Crisis Staff. It is pursuant to the decision of the Council for National Security of the Serbian Republic of BH on general mobilisation. And as we see above, it is received by Bratunac -- you see the stamp, by Bratunac on the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, I indicated that it was -- or the document indicates it was pursuant to the decision of the National Security Council on general mobilisation. In that connection if we could have 65 ter 02479.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a record of the session of the National Security Council of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the government held on the 27th of April, 1992. And if we look down the page at about the third paragraph it provides: "It was decided to conduct full-scale mobilisation ..." So, Mr. Stanic, the chronology was: Pale, that is, the NSC in this case, made a decision to conduct general or full-scale mobilisation. Birac acted on it two days later on the 29th of April, 1992, and that decision by the Birac region authorities was received by Bratunac the next day, on 30 April 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: If I may explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The previous document is a document which was wilfully signed by Miroslav Deronjic for Bratunac. There was no Crisis Staff that was formed in the region and it did not function or operate, and for that reason the document was processed or given a number only at the municipal Assembly in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to clarify quickly. Mr. Deronjic is another official on SAO Birac; right? We can find his name in one of the earlier documents as a member, I believe, of the Political Council?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I think that he was a deputy in the Assembly, but he was not a member of the Executive Board of the region. And he did not have the authority to form a Crisis Staff. I think we're talking about the Crisis Staff in the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I thought these documents you are tendering them to show the efficiency of communication, irrespective of the merits of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's exactly right. I was going to get to that point just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you can get to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thanks. And the issue about Deronjic and the Political Council will be resolved by the documents already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But the fact remains, Mr. Stanic, that Pale issued a decision on the 27th of April, 1992. It was received no later than the 29th of April. And it was disseminated that that decision in response to the Pale decision was disseminated and received by Bratunac, for example, a day later; that's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honour. I tender 65 ter 02479.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2479 receives number P7088, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7088 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stanic, this will be my last issue and it continues to focus on your assertion regarding both communication and how you attempted to resolve it by speaking with representatives of municipalities of adjacent or bordering municipalities, I take it. And let me put it to you simply in the interests of time and that is, Mr. Stanic, when you conferred with representatives of adjacent municipalities -- let me simplify it this way. You were aware of the policies of the republic level not only by your contact with representatives of other municipalities but also through direct contact with the highest leadership of Republika Srpska, and that occurred, among other things, during your meeting of June 30th, 1992, in Zvornik with Mr. Karadzic, General Mladic, and representatives of other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, the general policy of the Serbian Democratic Party I was familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at that meeting the representative from Bratunac advised the leadership that according to the -- and this is at page 258 of the English, page 256 of the B/C/S transcribed version - advised that: Although according to the last census it was 64/36 in favour of Muslims, "in Bratunac municipality we now have two Muslims." And the representative of Zvornik, Mr. Gruic, who was also a member of the Political Council of the Birac region, told Mr. Karadzic and General Mladic: "We have successfully implemented the president's decision to settle Divic and Kozluk with our children." And the TO -- that's at page 249 through 250 of the English, page 247 through 248 of the B/C/S transcribed version. And Marko Pavlovic, the TO commander in Zvornik, told Mr. Karadzic and General Mladic: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims." And noted further: "We had brought peace to Sepak, Divic, and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out while we demanded it." That was at pages 253 through 254 of the English, 251 through 252 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the transcript doesn't show the name of this document -- the title of the document that you're reading from. Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. That's P353, it's one of the Mladic notebooks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, contrary to the suggestion in your statement, you in fact not only had contact with municipal representatives, but contact with them in the presence of the republic-level leadership during which municipal representatives talked about their success in reducing the number of Muslims in their population and explained how active they were in evicting them. And that's the truth of what you knew about the policy, both from other representatives in municipalities and from republic leaders themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I only had two meetings with Radovan Karadzic in 1992. If that is good communication, then I agree with your assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's all I have, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stanic, you have spoken at length here about the work of the Executive Council of the Autonomous District of Birac. Can you tell us, according to your best recollection, when the last meeting of the Executive Council of the Autonomous District of Birac was held?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to give you the precise time. Roughly I can say that this was in mid-May 1992, after which activities ceased. And that's why I couldn't answer with a yes or a no. We were not divested of our posts, but we did not continue with our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And after this meeting in mid-May 1992 of the Executive Board of the Birac Autonomous Region, was there any other meeting held which you attended or did you hear of any other meeting being held?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: In that form as the Executive Council, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just for my clarity, is the Autonomous District the same thing as the Autonomous Region? Your first question related to Autonomous District. Now you're going to Autonomous Region. Are they the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it states "the Autonomous District," that's what it states in the heading. So I think so, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I would just seek one more answer from you. In your statement you talked about going to Tuzla and calling upon the Muslims from Vlasenica to return to Vlasenica. You also gave us the dates of when that was in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 14th or the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now the question: From that time until the 30th, when you were -- and until the 30th of May when you were calling upon Muslims to return to Vlasenica, did you ever receive any document in which it was suggested that the Muslim population in Vlasenica should be treated differently?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No, we did not get any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I thank you on behalf of General Mladic's Defence. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, just one more thing but we can do that once the witness leaves. We just need to resolve one technical issue that has cropped up and it has to do with a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll pay attention to it soon. Have the questions triggered any need for further questions? I may have one but I want to first carefully -- no, I leave it to that. Mr. Stanic, this concludes your evidence. I think everyone is happy that they could accommodate you in returning back home in time. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way and for having answered the questions, questions that were put to you by the parties, questions that were put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you had a practical matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one sentence, Your Honours. It seems to me that exhibit which was tendered by the Prosecution which got number P7087, P7087 completely corresponds to a Defence exhibit which was given number D885 today. So then we would have one document appearing under two different numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I'm -- well, I've looked at it quickly. That was a series of three documents. The document -- that may be right because I didn't refer to a D number on that. One document is the order by Dr. Karadzic for Mr. Djokanovic, that's June 10th. That was not in evidence as far as I'm aware. And I thought that was the only document in that series that we tendered, but I'd have to check. So I'm just wondering if there's a -- because -- and then the June 16th document that I think is the one that Mr. Stojanovic is referring to may sound similar but I don't think that got a new number. Perhaps I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And D885 was the first of the two associated exhibits under number 1D3128.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'm pretty sure that 65 ter 16217 was indeed the June 10th document and was not in evidence as I understand it. So I -- again, I referred to three documents, June 10th, June 16th, and June 17th, and only the first of those received a new number. So if that's the document that Mr. Stojanovic is referring to as a D number, then that's the problem, but I wasn't aware that was the case. D885, as I understand it, is the 16 June document. That may already have two documents because I cited -- no? Okay. Because I think it came up under a different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following: Have a cup of tea together with Mr. Stojanovic, find out what is there to be clarified for us, and at the same time one of the problems is striking and then getting back, that if someone later reads the transcript and has to find 20 pages later that what he reads was later changed, then sometimes the disadvantage of having the same document under two numbers is less than the disadvantage of being misled by something which hardly visible will change 20 pages later. So nevertheless, we would like to have on the record whether there are any duplicates, but whether that should be accompanied by any action is still to be considered. We adjourn for the day. The Chamber expresses its appreciation to the parties that they made it possible for the witness to return home. We resume Monday, the 2nd of February, that is in courtroom I, 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of February, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.20 p.m.,
